source_title_hint: Don’t Stretch Your Tight Psoas. Do This Instead
primary_summary: The video explains that a tight psoas often causes anterior pelvic tilt and hyperlordosis because the body's center of gravity is shifted forward. It recommends shifting the center of gravity back and improving pelvic rotation using a simple foam‑roller‑and‑wall drill, rather than stretching the psoas directly.

classification.usefulness_reason: Provides a clear biomechanical explanation and a concrete corrective protocol that can be applied without equipment beyond a foam roller and a wall.

problem_statements: A tight psoas pulls the pelvis forward, creating anterior pelvic tilt and excess lumbar lordosis.
Stretching the psoas alone does not address the underlying forward shift of the center of gravity.
habits_or_contexts: Standing posture with forward‑shifted center of gravity
key_visual_points: Feet hip‑width apart, shins parallel to floor
Three points of foot contact on wall (inner heel, big toe base, little toe base)

knowledge_units.title: Tight psoas creates anterior pelvic tilt
knowledge_units.summary: A tight psoas (hip flexor) pulls the pelvis forward, shifting the body's center of gravity anteriorly and leading to anterior pelvic tilt and hyperlordosis.
mechanisms: Hip flexor tension draws pelvis forward
Forward center of gravity reinforces tilt

knowledge_units.title: Foam‑roller thigh drill with wall foot positioning
knowledge_units.summary: Shift the center of gravity back and improve pelvic rotation by using a foam roller between the thighs while maintaining three points of foot contact against a wall.
execution_steps: Place feet hip‑width apart, shins parallel to the floor (≈48 s)
Insert a foam roller between the mid‑thighs (≈49 s)
Keep chin passively pointing toward the ceiling (≈53 s)
On the wall, feel contact at inner heel, base of big toe, and base of little toe (≈60 s)
Apply light pressure (1‑2/10 effort) into the wall with those points (≈66 s)
Maintain the position while breathing normally
cues: Focus on inner heel and big‑toe contact
when_useful: When psoas tightness causes anterior pelvic tilt
When posture shows forward‑shifted center of gravity
when_not_useful: If psoas tightness is due to acute injury requiring medical assessment

knowledge_units.title: Why the drill releases the psoas
knowledge_units.summary: The drill moves the pelvis backward and reduces hip‑flexor tension, allowing the psoas to relax because it no longer acts as a forward‑pulling force.
mechanisms: Pelvis positioned under the body reduces hip‑flexor stretch
Shifting CG backward decreases forward pull of psoas
